'''''Pilosocereus collinsii''''' is a species of cactus native to [[Oaxaca]], Mexico.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Pilosocereus collinsii (Britton & Rose) Byles & G.D.Rowley {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:196683-2 |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Pilosocereus collinsii'' grows up to 3 meters tall, having slender stems 3-4 cm in diameter. Each stem has around 7 obtuse ribs. Numerous acicular spines are found on the areoles; the areoles are spaced 1.5 cm apart. Up to 5 cm long, the flowers are born on the stem tips. Fruits are globular, somewhat depressed, and 3 cm long. The black seeds are 1.5 to 2 mm long.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last1=Britton |first1=Nathaniel |title=Cactaceae 4 |last2=Rose |first2=Joseph |date=December 24, 1923 |pages=353 |language=En}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
''Pilosocereus collinsii'' was originally described in 1923 as ''Cephalocereus collinsii'' by [[Nathaniel Lord Britton|Britton]] and Rose. ''Cephalocereus collinsii'' was then recombined, becoming the name ''Pilocereus collinsii''. Finally, ''Pilocereus'' was transferred to the current genus ''Pilosocereus'', resulting in the current name.<ref name=":0" /> Some sources consider ''Pilosocereus collinsii'' as a synonym of [[Pilosocereus purpusii|''Pilosocereus purpusii'']], however, most sources do not accept this treatment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pilosocereus collinsii |url=http://www.llifle.net/Encyclopedia/CACTI/Family/Cactaceae/6692/Pilosocereus_collinsii |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=www.llifle.net}}</ref>

== Etymology ==
The specific epithet "Collinsii" refers G. N. Collins, who first reported this plant in 1902.<ref name=":1" />
